subject: The condition of my mixed model contains an unknown parameter

messages.author: 5e0a072a41164542
messages.subject: The condition of my mixed model contains an unknown parameter
parts:
My mixed model is a little bit special. 
It has a term beta1*log[S(i)-X(i)], where X(i) comes form the observed data but S(i) is the parameters. Only if S(i)>X(i), the model works. 
Otherwise if I still have to write an expression, I can give an extremely large constant. 
i.e., my model is
y=beta0 + beta1*log[S(i)-X(i)] if S(i)>X(i), otherwise y=200

Note that f(y|parameters) can be written out ( i.e., the likelihood of y is known).

I explored the Stan manual 2.3.0, and found these ways:

1. In Chapter 21.5, Page 195, it gives us the conditional statements,  if (condition1)  statement1.... else statement2. 
    Each condition must be a real or integer value.
I'm wondering if I put the "if else" condition in the model part, will the Stan model work.
Or if it is possible to use the "While" statement. 

2. Since the likelihood is able to be written down, I'm also thinking to use the Log Probability Increment Statement, increment_log_prob.
    I found an example in the Manual Page 66, Section 9.2, it specifies
increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(log(0.3)+ normal_log(y,-1,2),
log(0.7)+ normal_log(y,3,1));

    Also in the FAQ https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/stan-users/4gv3fNCqSNk/VonPUkdcZuUJ
    To utilize the Kumaraswamy distribution, it uses log-likelihood:

// log-likelihood
  lp__ <- lp__ + N * (log(a) + log(b)) + (a - 1) * sum_log_x;
  for (i in 1:N) {
    summands[i] <- (b - 1) * log1m(pow(x[i],a)); // log1m(y) := log(1 - y)
  }
  lp__ <- lp__ + sum(summands); // faster than doing inside loop
(I believe in Stan version 2.3, it is replaced by statement increment_log_prob)

can I fit the above model in the same way?

I'll be really grateful if anybody can come up with some ideas.


Dora

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] The condition of my mixed model contains an unknown parameter
parts:
Stan doesn't give you an easy way to encode the constraint

S[i] > X[i]

when S is a parameter vector and X a vector computed from data.

The simplest way to program it is to use a parameterization:

vector<lower=0>[N] S_minus_X;

with your model term now implemented as

beta1 * log(S_minus_X[i]);

so that S_minus_X[i] is the amount which S[i] is above
X[i]. Then you can define S as a transformed parameter:

transformed parameters {
vector[N] S;

S[i] <- S_minus_X[i] + X[i];
}

But if you don't need to use S anywhere in the model, you're better of
defining it as a generated quantity.

Because it's only a linear increment with data, there's no Jacobian
adjustment needed.

You may want to use

multiply_log(a,b) = a * log(b)

where

multiply_log(beta1, S_minus_X[i]) = beta1 * log(S_minus_X[i]);

Some more comments below.

- Bob

On Jul 2, 2014, at 10:39 PM, Dora Zhou <zhou...@gmail.com> wrote:

> My mixed model is a little bit special.
> It has a term beta1*log[S(i)-X(i)], where X(i) comes form the observed data but S(i) is the parameters. Only if S(i)>X(i), the model works.
> Otherwise if I still have to write an expression, I can give an extremely large constant.
> i.e., my model is
> y=beta0 + beta1*log[S(i)-X(i)] if S(i)>X(i), otherwise y=200

This won't sample well --- you really want the support of
a parameter to match its constraints. Hence the parameterization
above.

>
> Note that f(y|parameters) can be written out ( i.e., the likelihood of y is known).
>
> I explored the Stan manual 2.3.0, and found these ways:
>
> 1. In Chapter 21.5, Page 195, it gives us the conditional statements, if (condition1) statement1.... else statement2.
> Each condition must be a real or integer value.
> I'm wondering if I put the "if else" condition in the model part, will the Stan model work.
> Or if it is possible to use the "While" statement.
The conditional won't work well --- see above.

> 2. Since the likelihood is able to be written down, I'm also thinking to use the Log Probability Increment Statement, increment_log_prob.
> I found an example in the Manual Page 66, Section 9.2, it specifies
> increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(log(0.3)+ normal_log(y,-1,2),
> log(0.7)+ normal_log(y,3,1));

This is fine, but you still need to make sure the parameters satisfy
the constraints. This example is for a mixture model.

>
> Also in the FAQ https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/stan-users/4gv3fNCqSNk/VonPUkdcZuUJ
> To utilize the Kumaraswamy distribution, it uses log-likelihood:
>
> // log-likelihood
> lp__ <- lp__ + N * (log(a) + log(b)) + (a - 1) * sum_log_x;
> for (i in 1:N) {
> summands[i] <- (b - 1) * log1m(pow(x[i],a)); // log1m(y) := log(1 - y)
> }
> lp__ <- lp__ + sum(summands); // faster than doing inside loop
> (I believe in Stan version 2.3, it is replaced by statement increment_log_prob)
> can I fit the above model in the same way?
I'm not sure what you're suggesting here.

>
> I'll be really grateful if anybody can come up with some ideas.
>
>
> Dora
